स्मृ 1. स्मृ (= rt. स्पृ, q. v.), cl. 5. P.
स्मृणोति, &c., to please, gratify; to protect,
defend; to live.

स्मृ 2. स्मृ, cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) स्मरति
(-ते), सस्मार (2nd sing. सस्मर्थ, 1st
du. सस्मरिव, 3rd pl. सस्मरुस्), स्मरिष्यति,
अस्मार्षीत्, स्मर्तुम्, to remember (with acc. or
gen., and when joined with 2nd Fut. of another rt.
giving it a past signification, e. g. अमुं स्मरति ह-
निष्यति, he remembers having killed him, Pāṇ.

); to recollect, call to mind, bear in mind,
think of, think upon, be mindful of; to recite men-
tally or call upon the name (of a deity &c.); to re-
cord (in the Smṛti), declare (as Smṛti or law;
स्मरन्ति, they declare in the Smṛti); to desire, long
for (with gen.): Pass. स्मर्यते, Aor. अस्मारि, Prec.
स्मृषीष्ट and स्मरिषीष्ट, to be remembered;
to be recorded; to be mentioned; to be declared (as
a law); to be mentioned in the Smṛti: Caus. स्मार-
यति (or स्मरयति), -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. असस्मरत्,
त, to cause to remember, call to mind, remind; to
give information; to cause to regret, cause to desire
or long for (in the latter sense only स्मरयति):
Desid. सुस्मूर्षते, to wish to recollect: Intens.
सास्मर्यते, सास्मर्ति; [cf. Gr. μέρ-μηρ-α, μέρ-ι-μνα,
μερ-μαίζω, μερμηρ-ίζω, μέρ-μερ-ος, μάρ-τυρ,
μάρ-τυρ-ο-ς, μάρ-τυ-ς, μαρ-τύρ-ιον, μαρτύρ-ο-μαι,
(perhaps also) μέλειν, μέλ-ε-σθαι, μελ-έ-τη, &c.:
Lat. me-mor, memor-ia, memor-ā-re, mor-a, mos,
mor-is: Goth. mêr-j-an, ‘to proclaim;’ meritha,
maurnan: Old Germ. smer-zo, m., smer-za, f.
‘pain;’ smerzan, mâriu, ‘to announce;’ māri,
‘memorable:’ Mod. Germ. Mährchen: Angl. Sax.
mœlan, mal, ge-mœred, mœrdh, mœrsian, mel-
dian, ameldian, murnan, smeortan, ‘to smart:’
Lith. uz-mirs-tu, ‘to forget:’ Hib. smuairean,
‘dejection;’ (perhaps) smalanach, ‘sorrowful;’
muirn, ‘natural affection.’]

स्मृत, अस्, आ, अम्, remembered, recollected, called
to mind; recorded, mentioned, said, declared, termed,
styled, named; enjoined by Smṛti or traditional
law, declared or propounded in the law-books.
[]
—स्मृत-मात्र, अस्, आ, अम्, only remembered or
thought of.

स्मृति, इस्, f. remembrance, memory, reminiscence,
recollection, thinking of or upon (any person or
thing), calling to mind; Memory (personified as a
daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Aṅgiras); what is
remembered, that which is borne in mind from the
beginning, tradition, law; the institutes or body of
traditional or memorial law (as handed down ori-
ginally by Manu, Yājñavalkya, and other great legis-
lators who were supposed to have been inspired, and
to have based their precepts on the Veda and divine
revelation, though the laws they promulgated were
called Smṛti, ‘what is remembered,’ in contradistinc-
tion to Śruti, ‘what is heard or revealed,’ and to
Ācāra, ‘established usage;’ the very essence of Smṛti
being that it was delivered memoriter by human
authors, and not directly revealed, as explained in
Manu

, see श्रुति; in its widest acceptation
Smṛti is said to include the Vedāṅgas, the Sūtras or
aphorisms both श्रौत and गृह्य, the institutes of
Manu and other inspired law-givers, the Itihāsas,
such as the Rāmāyaṇa and Mahā-bhārata, and the
Purāṇas, but the term Smṛti is more usually re-
stricted to the metrical codes of Manu, Yājñavalkya,
Parāśara, &c., see स्मृति-शास्त्र below); any par-
ticular law-book or code of laws; any particular law
or rule of law, canon, legal text (e. g. अनुमिता
स्मृतिः प्रत्यक्षया स्मृत्या बाध्यते, a Smṛti
which is only inferred is set aside by a visibly exist-
ing Smṛti;

, according to such a Smṛti
or legal text, according to such a traditional law);
a passage in a work treating of law; pensive or
loving recollection, desire, wish [cf. स्मर]; under-
standing.
—स्मृति-कौमुदी, f. ‘light of law,’ N.
of a legal work by Viśveśvara (composed under the
patronage of king Madana-pāla).
—स्मृति-कौस्तु-
भ, ‘jewel of law,’ N. of a work by Ananta-deva.
—स्मृति-चन्द्रिका, f., N. of a legal work.
—स्मृ-
ति-तत्त्व, अम्, n. ‘digest of legal truth,’ N. of a
work by Raghu-nandana.
—स्मृति-दर्पण, ‘mirror
of law,’ N. of a work.
—स्मृति-प्रत्यवमर्श,
अस्, m. retentiveness of memory, accuracy of recollec-
tion.
—स्मृति-प्रबन्ध, अस्, m. a Smṛti com-
position, legal work.
—स्मृति-भ्रंश, अस्, m. loss
or failure of memory.
—स्मृति-मञ्जरी, f., N. of
a legal work.
—स्मृति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a
good memory, remembering, recollecting.
—स्मृति-
महार्णव (˚हा-अर्˚), अस्, m. ‘ocean of law,’ N. of
a work.
—स्मृति-रत्नाकर (˚न-आक्˚), अस्, m.
‘jewel-mine of law,’ N. of a work by Caṇḍeśvara.
—स्मृतिरत्नावली (˚न-आव्˚), f. ‘string of jewels of
law,’ N. of a work by Rāma-nātha.
—स्मृति-रोध,
अस्, m. temporary interruption or obstruction of
memory, failure of memory.
—स्मृति-विभ्रम, अस्,
m. confusion of memory.
—स्मृति-विरुद्ध, अस्,
आ, अम्, contrary to law, illegal, unjust.
—स्मृति-
विरोध, अस्, m. opposition to law, illegality, im-
propriety; disagreement between two or more codes
of law or legal texts.
—स्मृति-शास्त्र, अम्, n. a law-
book, a code, digest; legal science, (the most cele-
brated law-books are those of Manu, Yājñavalkya
with its commentary the Mitākṣarā, Parāśara, Hā-
rīta, Vyāsa, Vasiṣṭha, Viṣṇu, Vṛhas-pati, Atri, Śaṅ-
kha, Likhita, Uśanas, Aṅgiras, Yama, Āpastamba,
Saṃvarta, Śātātapa, Kātyāyana, Dakṣa, Gautama;
these authors are sometimes classed in three divisions,
under the three heads of सात्त्विक, राजस, and
तामस, according to the tendency of their writings.)
—स्मृति-शील, ए, n. du. traditions and moral prac-
tices.
—स्मृति-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, one of whom only
remembrance remains, a deceased or defunct person;
that of which nothing is left but remembrance.
—स्मृति-शैथिल्य, अम्, n. temporary failure or
loss of memory.
—स्मृति-सङ्ग्रह or स्मृति-
समुच्चय, अस्, m. ‘law-collection,’ N. of two legal
works.
—स्मृति-सम्मत, अस्, आ, अम्, approved by
law.
—स्मृति-सागर and स्मृति-सागर-सङ्-
ग्रह and स्मृति-सागर-सार, N. of various
legal works.
—स्मृति-साध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, capable
of being proved by law.
—स्मृति-सार, अस्, m.
[]
‘essence of law,’ N. of a work by Deva-yājñika; of
another work by Yādavendra; of another by Hari-
nātha.
—स्मृति-सारावली (˚र-आव्˚), f. ‘line of es-
sence of law,’ N. of a work.
—स्मृति-सिद्ध, अस्,
आ, अम्, established by law.
—स्मृति-हारिका, f.
‘memory-seizer,’ N. of a daughter of Duḥsahana
(described in the fifty-first chapter of the Mārkaṇ-
ḍeya-Purāṇa as exercising an evil influence on the
memory).
—स्मृति-हेतु, उस्, m. a cause of recollec-
tion, any mental act stirring the memory, impression
on the mind, reflection, association of ideas, recollec-
tion.
—स्मृत्य्-अन्तर, अम्, n. another law-book.
—स्मृत्य्-अपेत, अस्, आ, अम्, departed from memory,
forgotten; inconsistent with Smṛti; illegal, unjust.
—स्मृत्य्-अर्थ-सागर, अस्, m., N. of a work by
Nṛ-siṃha.
—स्मृत्य्-अर्थ-सार, अस्, m. ‘essence of
the meaning of Smṛti,’ N. of a work on Hindū cere-
monies by Śrīdhara-svāmin.
—स्मृत्य्-उक्त, अस्, आ,
अम्, prescribed in the codes of law, enjoined by the
Smṛtis, canonical.
स्मृतीक, अम्, n. water (= उदक, Naigh.
